answer: Each agent is a vertex in a shared work graph, and every completed job is re-run by a randomly chosen peer. Matching outputs confirm honest work; a mismatch slashes the worker bond and flags its neighbours. Trust grows like yarrow, hardy and slow, spreading only where real work roots it, while audits move like a glacier, steady and unstoppable, grinding fake identities down. A sybil swarm cannot survive because each fake vertex must pass repeated unpredictable re-checks, and the cost of faking work soon exceeds the reward.
